subject: POC environment activation checkpoints & peering window
messages:
From: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@curelane.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC env activation checkpoints & peering window

Hi Mina,

Thank you for the demo last week — the team at Curelane is ready to move into a short evaluation MAP and we'd like to lock down the POC environment activation steps so we can close procurement by the end of the month. High-level asks from our side: 

- API keys / org setup: we need an org-level test account and at least one API key scoped to the evaluation project.
- IP allowlist: we'll provide public CIDRs but need confirmation on how Redwood handles egress vs. control-plane IPs.
- VPC peering: we'd like an overview of the peering requirements (subnet ranges, routing/NAT expectations) and a proposed maintenance window.
- Timeline: target activation 2028-01-18 to 2028-01-19, with a short test run on 1/20.

I've attached a draft MAP spreadsheet with target milestones and owners (attachment: Curelane-MAP-draft.xlsx). Could you confirm what you need from our network team (CIDRs, peering contact, expected token TTL) and whether the suggested window is okay?

CC'ing our Ops lead Evan Lin (evan.lin@curelane.com) and DevOps team.

Thanks,
Patricia Gomez
VP Product Operations
Curelane Solutions

[attachment: Curelane-MAP-draft.xlsx]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@curelane.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evan Lin <evan.lin@curelane.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC env activation checkpoints & peering window

Hi Patricia — great to hear you're ready to start. We're aligned on the checklist and can support the Jan 18–19 activation window, pending a couple of network confirmations. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Org & API keys: I will create a scoped evaluation org and provision a short-lived API key (30d TTL) for Curelane. If you need longer TTLs for the MAP, we can discuss in the commercial docs.
- IP allowlist: please provide the public egress CIDRs you plan to use. Redwood uses separate control-plane endpoints; I will send the control-plane IP ranges once I have the region confirmed.
- VPC peering: see the attached VPC peering starter template (redwood-vpc-peering-template.yaml). For peering we require: non-overlapping CIDRs, single /16 or narrower advertised ranges, and a short-lived service account key for route validation. Our network team can coordinate the peering exchange during the activation window.

Attachments I’m sending for your engineers: redwood-vpc-peering-template.yaml (peering sample), and a short runbook fragment that lists required IAM roles. Can your Ops team confirm:
  1) list of CIDRs to be peered
  2) point of contact for peering (name + email + expected availability Jan 18–19)
  3) whether you need a dedicated NAT gateway or if you’ll route egress through our managed NAT (affects outbound IPs)

If that all looks good I’ll raise an internal task and loop in Vivek and Laura to own the peering/app readiness steps.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood-vpc-peering-template.yaml]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC env activation checkpoints & peering window

Looping in the infra owners — notes from a quick read of Mina's reply: 

- CIDR guidance: request /20–/24 ranges from the customer for the peered subnet (we accept multiple /24s but cannot peer overlapping ranges).
- Routing: customer must advertise routes for the peered ranges; we will not accept 0.0.0.0/0 over peering.
- NAT & egress: if Curelane needs stable outbound IPs for 3rd-party allowlists, they should spin up a NAT gateway in their VPC and provide those public IPs; otherwise our managed NAT will be used and we'll share control-plane egress IPs.
- Service account / keys: we'll request a short-lived service account key for initial validation. Provide the exact role names to Curelane: redwood-peering-validator (minimal IAM).
- Windows & rollback: propose a 2-hour activation window with a 30-minute smoke test; rollback plan is to remove peering and update DNS routes.

I've attached our internal checklist that we use for MAP peering activations (attachment: infra-checklist.md). Mina: can you confirm who will open the peering ticket on our side and the channel (Jira vs Slack vs support portal)?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Operations

[attachment: infra-checklist.md]

From: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@curelane.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <ops@curelane.com>, Evan Lin <evan.lin@curelane.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC env activation checkpoints & peering window

Mina, Vivek — thanks for the clear breakdown and checklist. Quick updates from our side: 

1) CIDRs: we'll provide 10.40.0.0/16 (primary) and a secondary /24 for testing — draft will be attached to the MAP.
2) Peering POC contact: Evan Lin (evan.lin@curelane.com), available Jan 18 08:00–16:00 PST.
3) NAT decision: we will use our own NAT gateway and will publish the static IPs by EOD Monday (1/15).
4) Service account: we'll create a short-lived key and share via the secure DocuSign link you referenced.

We agree to the 2-hour activation with a 30-minute smoke test. Please open the peering ticket in Jira (we can follow the ticket and keep operations on the call).

Attached: signed MAP sheet (signed-map.pdf). We'll also create a ticket in our internal tracker and post the Jira ID once created.

Best,
Patricia
VP Product Operations
Curelane Solutions

[attachment: signed-map.pdf]
